Take this free CAT Set Theory online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The Set Theory chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Set Theory tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Set Theory

Venn diagrams, union–intersection formulae for two and three sets, and counting "exactly/at-least" cases.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • n(A∪B) = n(A)+n(B)−n(A∩B).
  • n(A∪B∪C) = Σn(A) − Σn(A∩B) + n(A∩B∩C).
  • A set of n elements has 2ⁿ subsets.
  • De Morgan: (A∪B)′ = A′∩B′.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Forgetting to add back n(A∩B∩C) in the three-set formula.
  • Confusing "exactly one" with "at least one".
  • Miscounting the neither region.

questions.q: In a class of 100, exactly 70 passed in at least one subject. 50 passed Subject 1, 48 passed Subject 2. If exactly 50 passed in exactly one subject, find n(S1∩S2).
In a survey of 500 people, 200 like brand X, 180 like Y, 160 like Z. X∩Y=70, Y∩Z=60, X∩Z=80, all three=30. What percentage like none of the brands?
A college has Drama (D), Music (M), Sports (S) clubs. n(D)=80, n(M)=70, n(S)=65, D∩M=25, M∩S=20, D∩S=22, all three=8. How many join exactly two clubs?
If n(A)=a, n(B)=b, and n(A∩B)=c, then n(A△B) in terms of a, b, c is:
Out of 100 students, 72 passed Mathematics, 55 passed Statistics. The number who failed in both is 8% of total students. Find n(M∩S).
questions.explanation: Failed both = 8% of 100 = 8; passed at least one = 92; n(M∩S) = 72+55-92 = 35.

questions.q: Three sets A, B, C partition U (120 elements total, all in at least one). n(A)=60, n(B)=50, n(C)=45, n(A∩B)=20, n(B∩C)=15, n(A∩B∩C)=5. Find n(A∩C).
n(A∪B∪C)=500, exactly two=120, exactly three=30, n(A)+n(B)+n(C)=700. Find n(A∩B)+n(B∩C)+n(A∩C).
Out of 50 students, 25 take Mathematics, 22 take Physics, 18 take Chemistry. M∩P=8, P∩C=6, M∩C=7, all three=3. How many take none of these subjects?
In a survey of 120 people, 12 like neither of two products A and B. The ratio of people who like only A: only B: both is 4:3:2. Find n(A).
In a survey of 500, 270 read X, 215 read Y, 185 read Z. X∩Y=85, Y∩Z=70, X∩Z=75, all three=35. 5% read none. How many read exactly two newspapers?

faq.q: What is the three-set inclusion–exclusion formula?
faq.a: n(A∪B∪C) = n(A)+n(B)+n(C) − n(A∩B) − n(B∩C) − n(C∩A) + n(A∩B∩C).
